parameter_rows: No Fintype or DecidableEq on polynomial variables.
Arbitrary finite n; verified generalIndex and genericDet.
Arbitrary commutative ring R with real RingSeminorm p; exact specialization packaged and compiled.
No nonnegativity hypothesis needed: empty case C^0=1; nonempty entry bounds supply nonnegative upper values as required.
Matrix.det needs square finite index and commutative ring; dropping commutativity/subtraction not supported by this determinant API.
Needed uniform entry estimate; no premise unused. Removing yields false bound already for1x1.
modern_rows: Use existing RingSeminorm R with explicit p 1 ≤ 1, not a new global norm instance; applies to multiple seminorms on same ring.
Finite sum/product estimate needs no convergence or topology.
Bounds an existing determinant; does not construct a universal object.
Replace MvPolynomial σ ℤ by arbitrary CommRing R; no domain, field, nontriviality or completeness required.
Numerical finite determinant bound has no categorical enrichment to preserve.
Replace Fin l by arbitrary Fintype n with DecidableEq; factorial and exponent use card n.
After det_apply the proof has zero MvPolynomial mentions. Every normOne occurrence is the size map or its abstract law witness. GenericDet and RingSeminorm specialization compile.

RingSeminorm is submultiplicative, not multiplicative AbsoluteValue. (X+1)(X-1)=X²-1 has length2 while factors have length2 each. Sup/Gauss norm, spectral determinant and field norm are different objects. Keep unit bound for empty index and unrestricted C.
strategy_rows: Entry estimates and real order do not encode ideal inclusions.
General RingSeminorm determinant factorial bound is the contribution; reuse Finset generic sum/product induction and Matrix.det_apply rather than another coefficient-specific bound.
infrastructure_rows: No global instance introduced; local evidence bundles existing laws in RingSeminorm.
Proof does not define a production reducible alias.
Proposed theorem states p M.det, with ordinary bundled-function application.
Generic probes quantify R and n independently in Type*.
Uses existing RingSeminorm FunLike coercion; no new coercion.
modern_verdict: Existing RingSeminorm determinant theorem independently useful; no foundational normOne change required.
